newsitem.title: USA: ARI Network Services sells new PC package.
newsitem.headline: ARI Network Services sells new PC package.

text.p: ARI Network Services Inc on Monday said it will start selling a personal computer software package, called Meppel, that lets firms use electronic data interchange (EDI) faster, cheaper and without learning EDI technology to track product ordering, distribution and invoicing.
The company said in a release that Meppel lets businesses send, receive and manage electronic documents using the ARI Network, a private intranet, or via the Internet.
It said the first customers are agricultural chemical distributors that use the new software to send product movement reports to, and receive invoices from, manufacturers.

Meppel, which will replace ARI's current AgEDI Plus DOS software, will cost from less than $3,000 to more than $5,000 per user. Current AgEDI Plus users can upgrade to Meppel at a discount, the firm said.
ARI Network provides standards-based, Internet-enabled electronic commerce services for certain companies and distribution channels.
ARI shares were trading at 2-1/2, up 1/8.
